findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the `summarize` subcommand already exists on `rebar.llm.usage_log`, or add building it to the enumerated changes so AC4's retrieval command is actually reachable.
evidence: 'Three surgical changes, no new sink' enumerates only record(), success-path shape, and default-sink wiring
Retrieval offers 'python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl # folded Markdown summary'
AC4: 'state the exact command or path that retrieves it, and prove it by retrieving one'
findings.finding: The retrieval command `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl` (AC4) presupposes a `summarize` CLI entry point that none of the three enumerated 'surgical changes' builds — the changes cover record()/success-path/default-sink but not a module __main__ or summarize subcommand.
findings.location: Fix plan 'Retrieval (acceptance criterion 4)' vs '### Three surgical changes'
scenarios: Executor implements the three changes, then finds `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize` does not exist and cannot satisfy AC4's 'prove it by retrieving one'
findings.suggested_fix: Either cite the existing `__main__`/summarize entry point, or add a fourth change that adds it; if only `cat .rebar/usage.jsonl` is guaranteed, make that the proving command for AC4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the lifecycle of `.rebar/usage.jsonl` — atomic line-append (single write() of a newline-terminated row) and a retire/rotation or documented unbounded-growth acceptance.
evidence: 'the repo-local <repo_root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl'
No mention of rotation, truncation, size bound, or cleanup
No mention of concurrent-append ordering when multiple gate runs write
findings.finding: `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is an append-only shared file with no defined RETIRE/rotation path and no stated concurrency handling for concurrent gate-session appends.
findings.location: Fix plan change 3 ('Gate runs record by default')
scenarios: Long-lived repo accumulates an unbounded usage.jsonl
Two gate runs (or parallel test workers) append concurrently and interleave partial lines
findings.suggested_fix: Write each row as a single newline-terminated append (O_APPEND line-atomic), and state whether/how the file is rotated or is expected to be transient local state cleaned by existing .rebar hygiene.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that a record()/write failure on the gate failure path is surfaced-but-non-masking (log-and-continue, never supersede the original exception).
evidence: 'the FAILURE path records it too ... is the case most likely to be missed'
No mention of guarding the file write so a record() IOError does not supersede the gate's own exception
findings.finding: The durable write on the FAILURE path has no stated error handling — a disk/IO error while recording is exactly the moment (budget exhaustion) the plan says the numbers are most needed, yet a throwing write could mask or replace the original gate failure.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria bullet 2 + fix plan change 2 (failure path feeds run_messages)
scenarios: A gate run raises its real failure; the appended record() write then raises IOError, obscuring the root failure
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the durable write so any exception is logged/swallowed relative to the primary control flow, ensuring the original gate outcome propagates unchanged.

scenarios: Operator reads docs:698-704, still cannot find the new usage log or the retrieval command

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Scope-note claim: the tool-filter predicate reads `run_ctx.run_step` (agent_call.py:70-71), not `run_ctx.usage` (which exists nowhere in src/rebar) — restate what is actually live, or cite the real source of per-run request/tool-call counts (failure_usage over accumulated pydantic-ai messages).
evidence: agent_call.py:70-71 — the only tool-filter predicate is `def available(run_ctx, _tool_def): return run_ctx.run_step <= limit` — it uses run_step, not usage.
search for `run_ctx.usage` and `ctx.usage` across src/rebar returned (no matches).

findings.location: Plan section 'Scope note' — sentence 'run_ctx.usage is live inside the tool-filter predicate.'
scenarios: An implementer following the Scope note looks for run_ctx.usage as an already-captured source and either wastes effort or mis-wires the source of the counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'run_ctx.usage is live inside the tool-filter predicate' with the accurate source: the per-run counts are derivable from the accumulated pydantic-ai messages via usage_log.failure_usage(); the tool-filter predicate itself only exposes run_ctx.run_step.

The gap section's own control-group question is per-epic (per-run), not per-op
findings.finding: The named retrieval command `usage_log summarize` cannot surface the newly-recorded shape fields, duration, or per-run counts: summarize() folds only _FIELDS (tokens+requests) grouped by `op` and never reads tool_calls/tool_calls_distinct/max_consecutive_repeat/duration_s/ticket, and it produces no per-run or per-ticket rollup. The sink is per-CALL (one row per LLM call), yet AC1/AC3 and the motivating question ('how many of 240 requests did the epic use?') are per-RUN. Neither `summarize` nor raw `cat` yields a per-run/per-ticket aggregate without manual re-summation.
findings.location: Fix plan 'Retrieval (acceptance criterion 4)'; usage_log.summarize() lines 468-577; AC1/AC3/AC4
scenarios: operator runs summarize on .rebar/usage.jsonl to answer 'did this gate loop or explore' and sees only token totals by prompt name
operator wants requests-used-vs-240 for one epic and finds rows keyed by op, not run/ticket, so must group by ticket manually
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `summarize` section (or a new subcommand) that groups rows by ticket/run and prints requests, tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, max_consecutive_repeat, and duration alongside the applicable limits, then point AC4's proof at that output.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that on the success path only the tool-call shape keys (tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, max_consecutive_repeat, top_repeated_tool_calls, finish_reason, request_limit, tool_calls_limit) are merged and that the token/request counts from _extract_usage remain authoritative (do not let failure_usage's `totals` overwrite them).
evidence: _extract_usage (structured_run.py:475-484) returns input/output/cache_read/cache_write/requests from pydantic-ai RunUsage — the authoritative, priced numbers
failure_usage (usage_log.py:159-191) ALSO returns those same keys via `totals`, counted from ModelResponse frames
docstring at usage_log.py:456-459 notes the library NORMALIZES cache token names — a frame-count re-derivation is not guaranteed to match

Fix plan says 'merges the shape into usage' without stating that only the shape keys (tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, max_consecutive_repeat, top_repeated_tool_calls, finish_reason, limits) are merged and the _extract_usage token/request values are preserved
findings.finding: The success-path instruction 'feeds those messages through the SAME usage_log.failure_usage() ... and merges the shape into `usage`' is under-specified on precedence and can corrupt existing billable telemetry: failure_usage() returns requests + the four token fields (its `totals`), and the success path already holds the authoritative counts from _extract_usage(run_result) (pydantic-ai RunUsage). A blind merge would overwrite RunUsage.requests/tokens with message-frame recomputations that can differ (the library normalizes and aggregates cache tokens; counting ModelResponse frames does not).
findings.location: Fix plan step 2 ('merges the shape into `usage` before record_call_spend')
scenarios: a normal success call: merged failure_usage overwrites usage['requests'] and usage['input_tokens'] with frame-derived values, and record_call_spend then persists/prices the wrong numbers
cache token disagreement makes est-cost pricing drift on the success path only
findings.suggested_fix: Merge with explicit key selection, e.g. `usage.update({k: shape[k] for k in _SHAPE_FIELDS if k in shape})`, and add a test asserting success-path usage['requests']/token fields equal _extract_usage's values, not the frame recount.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record enough to reconstruct rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0's windowed distinct-ratio (e.g. persist the ordered tool-call-signature sequence, or precompute and store the minimum trailing-window distinct-ratio), because the aggregate tool_calls_distinct / max_consecutive_repeat / top-5 fields in _SHAPE_FIELDS are provably blind to k-cycles and cannot yield a windowed ratio.
evidence: Plan AC3: 'at minimum the distinct-vs-total tool-call-signature counts, so the windowed distinct-ratio [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0] establishes can be computed from the record'

Plan step 1 _SHAPE_FIELDS = (tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, max_consecutive_repeat, top_repeated_tool_calls, request_limit, tool_calls_limit, finish_reason) — all aggregates; top_repeated_tool_calls is top-5 {signature,count}, carrying no ordering.

rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0: 'bf31 pre-fix ... a genuine loop ... overall distinct ratio 0.511 ... max_consecutive_repeat 1' vs 'c827 ... healthy breadth ... 0.922 ... 5' — proves both the overall distinct-ratio and max_consecutive_repeat point the WRONG way for a k-cycle; only 'lowest distinct-ratio across any trailing window' separates them.
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:213-234 _repetition_summary returns only counts/longest-adjacent-run/top-5 — the signature sequence is discarded, so a window cannot be reconstructed from a persisted row.
findings.finding: The record shape the plan persists (aggregate tool_calls_distinct, max_consecutive_repeat, and top-5 top_repeated_tool_calls) cannot yield the windowed distinct-ratio AC3 claims it enables, because a trailing-window ratio needs the ordered tool-call-signature sequence (or per-window set cardinalities) and none is recorded.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, bullet 3 ('distinguish a LOOP from genuine BREADTH ... the windowed distinct-ratio [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0] establishes can be computed from the record') and Fix plan step 1 (_SHAPE_FIELDS allowlist)
scenarios: An operator queries a recorded gate run to decide whether a 240-request run was a loop or breadth, but every persisted field is a whole-run aggregate blind to a 4-call cycle, so the tuning question the plan exists to answer remains unanswerable from the store.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend failure_usage()/_repetition_summary to also emit either the ordered signature list (privacy is already preserved — signatures are hashed) or a precomputed min-windowed-distinct-ratio field, add it to _SHAPE_FIELDS, and update AC3's wording to name the field that actually makes the windowed ratio recoverable.
